approach: Because the author repository is 404, this is a paper-only reimplementation. I will first try to recover the original 100-station CSV via Wayback/GitHub archive; if unavailable, I will reconstruct a real 100-station Istanbul EV charging set from OSM Overpass with an OpenChargeMap fallback, save it, and use a local equirectangular km projection. The primary C1 run follows the paper protocol exactly: custom random-init K-means (k=5, max 10 iterations), GA TSP inside each cluster, cluster-order GA (mutation 0.10, 100 iterations, population 100), open-route concatenation, seed 42. I will also compute the C2/C4 sequential baseline, C3 distance-derived duration, C5 Eq. 3 improvement, seed-stability diagnostics, and an interactive map. All deviations and the paper's C5 inconsistency (417.53->308.49 is 26.1%, not 35%) will be written to results/metrics.json.

files.purpose: Pinned Python dependencies: numpy, pandas, requests, tqdm, matplotlib, folium, gmplot.
Fetch arxiv HTML/PDF and parse Table 3 configurations if available; otherwise return the fully specified target configuration as the only runnable config.
Single source of truth for all hyperparameters, paths, seeds, Table 3 configs, and documented assumptions.

Recover the original 100-station CSV from archive if possible, else fetch real Istanbul EV charging stations from OSM Overpass/OpenChargeMap, deduplicate, select exactly 100, validate, and write data/stations.csv.
Project lat/lon to local equirectangular km coordinates, build the 100x100 symmetric distance matrix, and compute dataset-order sequential route distance.
Custom K-means with random distinct-point initialization, nearest-centroid Euclidean assignment, mean updates, convergence/iteration limit, and empty-cluster reseeding.
Permutation genetic algorithm with tournament selection, order crossover, swap mutation, elitism; used both for intra-cluster TSP-style routing and cluster-order optimization.

Assemble intra-cluster routes, optimize cluster order, concatenate into the final open route, compute total distance/duration/improvement, and expose diagnostics including orientation-minimized variant.
Render cluster-colored stations and final route lines to results/route_map.html using gmplot if an API key exists, else folium/OSM as a documented deviation.
Single entrypoint: orchestrates data acquisition, K-means, intra-cluster GA, cluster-order GA, baselines, stability runs, visualization, and writes results/metrics.json.

config.data_order: archive CSV order if recovered; otherwise deterministic sort by (name, lat, lon) of selected OSM records (A6)
config.kmeans_init: random distinct data points with fixed seed (paper R3; A1)
config.distance_projection: local equirectangular to km using mean latitude; R=6371.0088 km (A5)
config.intra_cluster_solver: GA TSP per cluster with pop=100, iters=100, mutation=0.10, elitism=2, followed by 2-opt polish (A2)
config.primary_orientation_policy: append each cluster route as returned (A11); also compute an orientation-minimized diagnostic without changing intra-cluster order
config.duration_speed_kmph: 35.48 (derived from paper C2/C4: 417.53 km / 706.22 min * 60; A9)
config.table3_configs: parsed from arxiv HTML/PDF via src/paper_tables.py; fallback [target config] (R9)
config.map_backend: gmplot if GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is set, else folium OpenStreetMap HTML (R12/R13; documented deviation)
config.smoke_subset: 12 stations, k=2, kmeans_iter=2, GA pop=10, GA iter=5 (smoke only)

steps: Create directories data/, data/raw/, results/ and install dependencies with `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
Run src/paper_tables.py to extract Table 3 configurations from the arxiv HTML/PDF; if extraction fails, record that only the fully specified target configuration is runnable.

Acquire the station table: try Wayback/GitHub-archive recovery of oyenigun/RouteOptimization CSV; if that fails, query OSM Overpass for amenity=charging_station in the Istanbul bbox, expand the bbox in documented steps if fewer than 100 unique EV stations are found, and fall back to OpenChargeMap if needed.

Extract id, name, latitude, longitude; deduplicate by rounded coordinates; sort deterministically by (name, lat, lon); keep exactly 100 rows; validate names, coordinates, and Istanbul bbox; write data/stations.csv.
Load stations and build local equirectangular km coordinates: x = R*cos(lat0)*radians(lon-lon0), y = R*radians(lat-lat0), with lat0/lon0 the mean coordinates.
Build the 100x100 Euclidean distance matrix and compute the sequential reference distance C2 as the sum of distances between consecutive rows in data/stations.csv order.
Compute C4 duration proxy as C2 distance divided by 35.48 km/h times 60, and record that the paper gives no duration formula.

Run the primary K-means configuration: k=5, random distinct-point initialization with seed 42, nearest-centroid assignment, mean updates, stop at convergence or 10 iterations; record labels, centroids, iteration count, and cluster sizes.

For each K-means cluster, run the intra-cluster GA TSP on the cluster's distance submatrix with open paths (no return), seed 42+cluster_id, population 100, 100 iterations, mutation 0.10, elitism 2, followed by 2-opt polish; record each cluster route and length.

Run the cluster-order GA over the 5 cluster labels with population 100, 100 iterations, mutation 0.10, tournament size 3, order crossover, swap mutation, elitism 2, seed 42; fitness is the total concatenated route distance including inter-cluster gaps.
As a check, enumerate all 5! = 120 cluster orders and verify the GA result equals the enumerated best order or record the gap.

Build the primary final route by concatenating each cluster's intra-cluster route in the GA-best cluster order without reversing cluster paths (A11), and compute C1 total distance. Also build an orientation-minimized diagnostic that may reverse each cluster path to reduce inter-cluster gaps, keeping it separate from the primary.

Compute C3 duration proxy as C1 distance divided by 35.48 km/h times 60, and compute C5 improvement with Eq. 3: 100*(C2-C1)/C2; also record the paper-table-implied improvement 100*(417.53-308.49)/417.53 = 26.1% and flag the paper's 35% claim as inconsistent.
Run stability diagnostics with seeds 123, 7, 2024, and if Table 3 has other configs, run the generic sweep; report mean/std/min/max but keep seed 42 as the primary C1.
Generate results/route_map.html with cluster colors and the final route polyline using gmplot if GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY exists, else folium/OSM; also save a static PNG if matplotlib is available.
Write results/metrics.json with C1-C5 values, targets, relative errors, tolerance flags, the exact run configuration, data provenance, and all documented deviations/assumptions.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke` using the first 12 stations, k=2, kmeans iterations=2, GA population=10, GA iterations=5, mutation=0.10, seed=42; assert that every selected station appears exactly once in the final route, all distances are finite, C2/C1/C5 are computed, and results/smoke_metrics.json is written. The smoke run should finish in under 10 seconds.
intermediate_checks: Data check: exactly 100 stations, unique rounded coordinates, non-empty names, all lat/lon inside the Istanbul bbox, and no missing values.

Distance check: matrix is symmetric, diagonal is zero, maximum pairwise distance is plausible for Istanbul, and sequential C2 is finite; compare to the paper's 417.53 km and flag data-order dependence.
K-means check: all 5 clusters are non-empty, labels sum to 100, centroids remain inside the bbox, inertia decreases or stays flat, and iterations used <= 10.

Intra-cluster route check: every station appears exactly once across all cluster routes; each cluster route length is <= the dataset-order path through the same cluster (sanity that optimization is not worse).
Cluster-order GA check: GA-best fitness <= the label-order concatenation; enumerate all 120 permutations and confirm the GA best is globally optimal or record the suboptimality gap.

Final route check: recompute C1 manually from the ordered station coordinates, confirm it equals the reported sum of intra-cluster plus inter-cluster distances, and confirm the route is open (no return leg).
Duration check: C4 proxy uses C2 and C3 proxy uses C1 at 35.48 km/h; compare both to 706.22 and 568.15 minutes and document that these are distance-derived, not Google road durations.
Improvement check: computed C5 is 100*(C2-C1)/C2; if C2 and C1 are near paper values, confirm it is ~26.1%, not 35%, and flag the paper's inconsistency.
Seed-stability check: run seeds 42, 123, 7, 2024 and report C1 spread; the primary remains seed 42, but a wide spread should be reported as seed sensitivity.
Tolerance check: C1 relative error band is 10%, i.e. [277.64, 339.34] km; if outside, inspect the orientation-minimized diagnostic and data-source deviations rather than tuning to the target.
budget_plan: Total ~25 minutes: 4 min setup/pip/Table 3 parse; 7 min archive/OSM data fetch, selection, validation, and distance matrix; 2 min smoke test; 5 min primary run plus 5! order enumeration and 3-seed stability; 4 min visualization and intermediate checks; 3 min writing results/metrics.json and documenting deviations.
